newsitem.title: UK: IEA sees first oil stock surplus for 18 months.
newsitem.headline: IEA sees first oil stock surplus for 18 months.

text.p: Oil inventories in the world's leading industrial nations recovered in January, ending the month higher than a year before for the first time in 18 months, the International Energy Agency (IEA) said on Friday.
The OECD's energy watchdog said stocks were drawn down by a modest 100,000 barrels per day (bpd) in January, compared with a decline of one million bpd in the same month last year.

"As a result, total stocks ended the month higher than a year before for the first time since July 1995, with distillate stocks being 14 million barrels higher," the Paris-based agency said in its monthly Oil Market Report.

The IEA maintained its forecast of world demand at 73.7 million bpd in 1997, up 1.9 million bpd, but increased its estimate of the call on OPEC crude plus stocks by 100,000 bpd to 25.4 million because of slightly lower than expected growth in non-OPEC supply.

"Non-OPEC supply growth was inhibited by abnormal weather and technical problems in January and February in the North Sea, Australia and the U.S. Gulf of Mexico, leading to a 300,000 bpd downward revision in the first quarter 1997 supply estimate," the agency said.
Non-OPEC supply growth for the second quarter was also revised down by 100,000 bpd.
